title: 6.1 A 3-Stacked Hybrid-Shutter CMOS Image Sensor with Switchable 1.2µm-Pitch 50Mpixel Rolling Shutter and 2.4µm-Pitch 12.5Mpixel Global Shutter Modes for Mobile Applications
problem: Rolling-shutter CMOS image sensors achieve high pixel density but suffer flicker artifacts and motion distortion, while global-shutter sensors eliminate these issues but exhibit higher random noise due to sampling capacitor design, forcing a choice rather than flexibility.
motivation: Mobile imaging demands 50+ megapixel resolution with flexibility between high-resolution rolling-shutter mode (fast-moving objects, low flicker) and global-shutter mode (no motion distortion, no flicker banding), requiring mode-switchable designs.
method: 3-layer stacked CMOS image sensor combining tight 1.2µm pixel pitch rolling-shutter (50Mp) with switchable 2.4µm pixel pitch global-shutter (12.5Mp) mode using hybrid shutter architecture and advanced stacking process.
key_novelty: Hybrid-shutter mode switching within single sensor enabling both high-resolution rolling-shutter and lower-resolution global-shutter on demand, rather than separate designs.
contributions: 50Mpixel rolling-shutter mode with 1.2µm pitch for high-resolution capture
12.5Mpixel global-shutter mode with 2.4µm pitch for motion-distortion-free imaging
Switchable modes addressing flicker, motion blur, and flash-banding issues
3-layer stacking enabling simultaneous storage and readout optimization
primary_theme: switchable hybrid-shutter image sensor for flexible mobile photography
